# Clean contact records: Slack for capture forms

**Pattern:** Data Enrichment · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers capture-forms work end to end across Slack, Google Sheets, HubSpot and Notion.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Init Cursor
3. Page Loop
4. Fetch Page from API
5. Split Result Items
6. Normalize Page Items
7. Remove Duplicate Leads
8. Upsert Harvest into Google Sheets
9. Tally Harvest Stats
10. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
11. Record Sub-workflow Result
12. Enrich with Reference Data
13. Fold In Enrichment Fields
14. Load Previous Snapshot
15. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
16. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
17. Archive Row Snapshot
18. Stamp Completion Time
19. Persist Run Metadata
20. Fingerprint for Idempotency
21. Drop Already-Processed Items
22. Guard Non-Empty email
23. Sort Leads Newest First
24. Cap Batch Volume
25. Stamp Processing Time
26. Tag Pipeline Metadata
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Notion)
29. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing capture-forms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Init Cursor → Page Loop → Fetch Page from API → Split Result Items → Normalize Page Items → Remove Duplicate Leads → Upsert Harvest into Google Sheets → Tally Harvest Stats → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Guard Non-Empty email → Sort Leads Newest First → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for capture forms
- A backlog too large to push into Slack in one pass, across 32 nodes
- Capture forms work where "Init Cursor" is still a manual step before Slack
- Capture forms work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for capture forms, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this capture-forms build
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this capture-forms build
- Batches the work so Slack rate limits never break a capture-forms run
- Every capture-forms run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Notion integration token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Split In Batches drives the pagination loop instead of a fixed number of HTTP calls, because the page count isn't known upfront — the loop output feeds back into itself until the source stops returning data. Fetching one page per iteration, not all pages at once, keeps memory bounded even against a source with tens of thousands of records.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Change the page-size parameter and watch how many loop iterations it takes to finish.
2. Add a hard cap (a Limit node) so a runaway source can't loop forever.
3. Point the fetch target at a real paginated API and adjust the cursor logic to match its response shape.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**The loop runs forever or exits immediately**
Cause: The loop output and the done output are wired the wrong way round.
Fix: Output 2 is the loop body; output 1 fires after the last batch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## ⏱ Rate limiting

Work is batched and spaced with Wait so provider quotas aren't tripped. If you hit 429s, lower the batch size or raise the wait — throughput drops, reliability rises.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your capture forms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
capture-forms payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
